answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: proof of unique storage. At registration each identity is assigned a distinct random dataset it must keep and prove it holds during periodic audits, challenged like a comet that returns on schedule. Honest agents each store their own slice. An attacker spinning up a thousand fakes must physically store a thousand distinct datasets; the data cannot be deduplicated or shared across an island of clones. Each audit sends a ripple that any missing store fails, so sybil scale is bounded by real disk, a cost that grows one to one with every fake.
